title: IonQ and Sandia National Laboratories Sign MOU to Accelerate Quantum Co-Design for National Security Applications - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IonQ signed an MOU with Sandia National Laboratories to co-design trapped-ion hardware, silicon photonics integration, and software for U.S. national security use cases at Sandia's Quantum Demonstration Facility in New Mexico, extending a relationship dating back to Sandia fabricating IonQ's original trapped-ion chips.

themes.theme: Government partnership and national security positioning

insights.claim: IonQ (NYSE: IONQ) signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Sandia National Laboratories to pursue co-design of quantum information science technologies for U.S. national security applications, operating out of Sandia's Quantum Demonstration Facility in New Mexico.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A formal MOU with a national lab embeds IonQ deeper into U.S. defense/national-security quantum procurement pipelines, a positioning edge versus competitors lacking equivalent government lab relationships.
insights.quote: Quantum platform developer IonQ (NYSE: IONQ) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Sandia National Laboratories to pursue the co-design of quantum information science (QIS) technologies for U.S. national security applications.

insights.claim: The partnership will align trapped-ion hardware development, silicon photonics integration, and software optimization with mission-relevant government use cases, with IonQ's hardware and application engineering teams working alongside Sandia scientists on system optimization, device characterization, and testing protocols.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals IonQ's roadmap explicitly folding silicon photonics integration alongside its core trapped-ion architecture, relevant for tracking whether IonQ pursues a hybrid hardware strategy versus pure trapped-ion scaling.
insights.quote: the public-private partnership will align trapped-ion hardware development, silicon photonics integration, and software optimization with mission-relevant government use cases.
insights.locator: Operating out of Sandia's Quantum Demonstration Facility

insights.claim: Sandia fabricated the original trapped-ion chips used in IonQ's earliest quantum processing units (QPUs), meaning the new MOU builds on and formalizes an existing historical technical relationship between the two organizations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The pre-existing supply relationship (Sandia as an original chip fabricator for IonQ) reduces execution risk on the new co-design partnership since the two organizations already have working technical familiarity.
insights.quote: Sandia fabricated the original trapped-ion chips utilized in IonQ’s earliest quantum processing units (QPUs).
insights.locator: The collaboration builds on a historical foundation

insights.claim: A central priority of the MOU is pairing Sandia's expertise in microfabrication and integrated silicon photonics with IonQ's QPU architecture to accelerate system scaling and enable high-fidelity quantum networking interconnects.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Highlights quantum networking interconnects as an explicit near-term technical goal for IonQ, a capability increasingly viewed as a bottleneck for scaling trapped-ion systems beyond single-module qubit counts.
insights.quote: A central priority of the initiative is pairing Sandia’s expertise in microfabrication and integrated silicon photonics with IonQ’s QPU architecture to accelerate system scaling and facilitate high-fidelity quantum networking interconnects.
insights.locator: Under the expanded scope of the MOU

insights.claim: By establishing a direct collaborative presence at Sandia's New Mexico facility, IonQ expands its geographic footprint into the state's growing defense and national laboratory quantum ecosystem, supporting federal mandates to maintain domestic leadership in quantum computing, secure networking, and defense infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Geographic expansion into New Mexico's defense-lab cluster positions IonQ to capture federal quantum spending tied to domestic-leadership mandates, a durable government demand channel distinct from commercial cloud revenue.
insights.quote: By establishing a direct collaborative presence at the New Mexico facility, IonQ expands its geographic footprint into the state’s growing defense and national laboratory quantum ecosystem
